When you replace what makes people valuable and it become cheaper across the board they will be replaced. There are only so many things that people value for the human experience, and these experiences are the only places I can imagine human labor remaining in an endgame of this economy.

The point about the legal profession is a very pertinent one. I dare to claim that I have some experience in both the legal profession (I'm in a litigation job now), but I'm also a hobby coder, long before there were any large language models. If you've used AI in the legal field, you will know that it lacks the balanced razor sharp reasoning in legal arguments. It either swings one side or the other, as if overinterpreting to justify a position it already took or was asked to take. Invariably dismisses arguments for the contrary and overblows the arguments for its position. If you prompt it to be more judgemental and consider both sides of the legal argument, it positions itself straight in the middle, with no nuance on either side. So, its legal argumentation is one of three discrete positions: 1. Full one side argumentation 2. Full other side argumentation 3. Straight in the middle of both argumentations It's more like a moot court submission by a 12 year old than even an intern.
